{'index': 0, 'translation': "Next month the 26th marks the one-year anniversary of the Tai Po Wang Fuk Court fire. The independent committee investigating the fire is expected to submit its report to the Chief Executive before the end of October. Recent media reports have indicated that the government has activated the Heads of Department Accountability System to investigate administrative responsibility for the fire and has transferred political assistants to assist. Chief Executive John Lee today (the 6th) did not respond to whether the mechanism has been activated, stating that the government has made a series of arrangements and will push forward reforms and accountability as soon as possible after the report is submitted. The luxury residence One Stanley in Stanley was exposed for reinforcing steel not matching the plans. Lee said the Buildings Department is investigating the case and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the investigation. With multiple projects being exposed for problems one after another, he said he attaches great importance to the construction quality of building works in Hong Kong, which concerns the professionalism, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will strictly enforce the law."}

{'index': 1, 'translation': 'It is nearly a year since the Wang Fuk Court fire. The independent committee is expected to submit its report before the end of October. (File photo)'}

{'index': 2, 'translation': 'Earlier media reports stated that two political assistants—former Deputy Secretary for Security Mohandas Alagiah, and Commissioner for Sports Choi Kin-pan—will provide support work at the investigation小组 under the Public Service Commission, specifically responsible for preliminary work on administrative accountability.'}

{'index': 3, 'translation': 'Chief Executive John Lee attended a press session before the Executive Council meeting today. When asked whether the matter was true, and whether activating the Heads of Department Accountability System to investigate responsibility means that even with a report, if official accountability is involved there will not be immediate results, and how long the public has to wait?'}

{'index': 4, 'translation': 'Lee stated that he made clear from the start that after the independent committee submits its report, he will actively study and follow up on the recommendations, carry out reforms and announce details. He did not directly respond to whether political assistants have already been transferred to prepare for preliminary investigation work, only saying that "the government has made a series of arrangements during this period," emphasising that after the report is submitted, based on its content, he will "push forward comprehensive reforms and pursue accountability as soon as possible in the short term," and detailed announcements will be made at that time.'}

{'index': 5, 'translation': "Lee stated that after the independent committee submits its report, reforms and accountability will be pushed forward as soon as possible according to the report's content. (File photo)"}

{'index': 6, 'translation': "Lee also reiterated several times that improvement measures are urgent. Therefore, when delivering the Policy Address in September, he announced 7 priority improvement measures, including prohibiting smoking at construction sites, strengthening regulation of fire service installations, strengthening disciplinary action and punishment for professionals and contractors, improving compliance operation of owners' corporations, studying criminalisation of bid-rigging, providing tendering and evaluation services for the first time, formulating pre-qualification lists for consultants and contractors, and researching solutions to better assist the public on projects involving professional expertise."}

{'index': 7, 'translation': 'According to records, the Public Service Commission is an independent statutory advisory body that advises the Chief Executive on matters relating to the appointment, promotion and discipline of civil servants. The Heads of Department Accountability System was introduced by Chief Executive John Lee in last year\'s Policy Address, establishing a two-tier investigation mechanism based on the severity of departmental issues. If the issue is less serious in nature, or is an isolated incident, the first-tier investigation will be conducted by the head of department. If the department has serious problems, or involves extensive, repetitive systemic issues, or may involve the role of the head of department, a second-tier investigation will be conducted by an investigation小组 led by the "Public Service Commission."'}

{'index': 8, 'translation': "The luxury residence One Stanley was exposed for having units with reinforcing steel not matching the plans. Lee said he would not comment on cases still under investigation, and has asked the Development Bureau to monitor the Buildings Department's investigation."}

{'index': 9, 'translation': 'One Stanley "steel reinforcement issue" — Development Bureau required to monitor investigation'}

{'index': 10, 'translation': 'Recently, building works have been exposed for problems one after another, including lift shaft tilting at the new block of Queen Mary Hospital, concrete samples at a Tung Chung public housing estate not meeting strength standards, and floor slab reinforcing steel at luxury residence One Stanley in Stanley not matching the plans. Lee was asked whether there are problems with construction and even project supervision?'}

{'index': 11, 'translation': 'Responding to the One Stanley project issue, he stated that the Buildings Department is seriously investigating the case, "ascertaining whether construction quality and supervision have been adequate, and will handle it strictly according to the law." As the investigation is still ongoing, he would not comment on the case details, and has asked the Development Bureau to monitor the case investigation. He nevertheless stressed that he attaches importance to the construction quality of building works in Hong Kong, "paying attention to whether professionals related to the project have performed their supervisory duties diligently, and whether contractors have violated regulations during construction," and pointed out that it concerns the professionalism, quality and safety of Hong Kong\'s construction industry, and the government will inevitably enforce the law strictly.'}

{'index': 12, 'translation': "He has also asked the Development Bureau to enhance regulatory requirements and penalties in legal aspects for overall building works, ensure the deterrent effect of legislation, severely punish relevant personnel who violate regulations, and safeguard the professionalism, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry. The Development Bureau will submit proposed amendments to the Buildings Ordinance this year to strengthen supervision and enhance the penalty system and sanctions. The authorities will push forward the relevant work at full speed."}

{'index': 13, 'translation': 'Recent concerns have been raised about nursing graduates facing difficulties finding jobs. Lee stated that demand for nurses has long existed, and pointed out that the Hospital Authority currently has over 3,000 nurse vacancies, which graduates can apply for. (File photo)'}

{'index': 14, 'translation': 'Executive Council member Tommy Cheung criticises "unions impersonating people" — Lee states demand has long existed'}

{'index': 15, 'translation': 'Discussions about nurses\' difficulty finding jobs have heated up recently. The source was a phone-in programme on a radio station after the Policy Address, during which a Mr. Kwok, who claimed to be a psychiatric nurse in a disciplinary force, said his application for deferred retirement was not approved, and that his nursing graduate daughter was unemployed upon graduation, questioning the Hospital Authority\'s recruitment of Mainland medical staff. Executive Council member Tommy Cheung subsequently questioned whether the unions were "possibly impersonating people making phone calls," and expressed his wholehearted support for importing foreign talent.'}

{'index': 16, 'translation': 'Reporters asked about nursing graduates\' difficulty finding jobs, how to address the concentration of vacancies among experienced nurses, and how to respond to the Executive Council member\'s remarks being criticised for intensifying social conflicts. Lee stated that in every industry, there are cases where graduates do not immediately seek employment for individual reasons, or where recruiting organisations select those most suitable for their needs, "resulting in situations where certain individuals are not hired." He emphasised that societal demand for nurses has always existed, especially given Hong Kong\'s continuous medical development and the trend of an ageing population, "so recruitment numbers will ultimately inevitably reflect these existing demands." He also said, without naming anyone, that "there are different discussions in society on this aspect, allowing everyone to discuss the issue more clearly."'}

{'index': 17, 'translation': 'Lee also pointed out that according to figures for 2025/26, there are approximately 4,000 potential nursing graduates, with about 2,500 actually applying to the Hospital Authority, meaning 1,500 are applying for positions outside the Hospital Authority. The Hospital Authority currently still has over 3,000 nurse vacancies, "nursing graduates can apply, and there is a chance of being hired."'}

{'index': 18, 'translation': 'Secretary for Health Professor Lo Chung-mau earlier在接受 multiple media interviews, clarifying that the government\'s recruitment policy definitely prioritises local talent. Lee also reiterated that according to the Hospital Authority\'s existing number of nurses, "99.8% are Hong Kong locally trained nurses," clearly implementing the local-talent-first employment policy. He also pointed out that currently 40% of nurses work in the public healthcare system, and the remaining 60% work in other healthcare positions, such as community nursing, elderly care, rehabilitation services, and private medical institutions. He emphasised that societal demand for nurses has long existed. The government will, according to healthcare service needs, exchange views with the industry and academia, and do a good job in planning for medical and healthcare training and manpower development.'}
